Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire from 1523 to 1536. Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha (c. 1495 – 15 March 1536), was the first grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire appointed by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.

Governing France during the childhood of Louis XV, whom he was related to as both great-nephew and first cousin twice removed, this early 18th-century regent married a daughter of Louis XIV — who is he?
Philippe II, Duke of Orléans: Regent of France from 1715 to 1723.
What single word names the practice of banning by law the making, selling, and drinking of alcoholic beverages?
The oldest of 14 children born to Palestinian immigrants in Detroit, this congresswoman became the first Palestinian American woman elected to Congress in 2018 — who is she?
Rashida Tlaib: American politician and lawyer (born 1976)
Co-leading Germany's Greens alongside Annalena Baerbock, this politician served as Vice Chancellor and climate minister under Chancellor Olaf Scholz — who is he?

Over three days in September 1982, Lebanese Forces militiamen — backed by the IDF — killed thousands of mostly Palestinian and Shia civilians in a Beirut neighbourhood and adjacent refugee camp; what is this atrocity called?
Sabra and Shatila massacre: 1982 mass murder of civilians in Beirut, Lebanon.
This Finnish lawyer chaired the National Coalition Party from 1994 to 2001 and later served as president from 2012 to 2024, defeating Pekka Haavisto in a 2012 runoff — who is he?
Sauli Niinistö: President of Finland from 2012 to 2024. Sauli Väinämö Niinistö (born 24 August 1948) is a Finnish politician who served as the president of Finland from 2012 to 2024.
Centered on Marib and Sirwah in what's now Yemen, this ancient kingdom was considered the birthplace of South Arabian civilization and once expanded into the Horn of Africa. Which kingdom?
Sheba: Ancient South Arabian kingdom. Sheba, or Saba, was an ancient South Arabian kingdom that existed in Yemen before 275 CE.
An architect by training who once served as mayor of Quito, this man won Ecuador's presidency on his third try in 1992 after founding a new conservative party — who is it?
Sixto Durán Ballén: President of Ecuador from 1992 to 1996.
Established by Seljuk Turks after their victory over Byzantine forces at Manzikert in 1071, this Turco-Persian state is considered the beginning of Turkish history in Anatolia. What was it?
Sultanate of Rum: Turkish state in central Anatolia from 1077 to 1308.
This biblical figure, son of Nahor, is best known as the father of the patriarch Abraham in the Book of Genesis — who is he?
Terah: Figure in the Hebrew Bible; son of Nahor.
The eighth shogun of his family's shogunate, ruling from 1716 to 1745, this samurai is remembered for repealing Japan's ban on Western literature — who was he?
Tokugawa Yoshimune: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1716 to 1745.

Exemplified by thinkers like Saint-Simon, Fourier, and Robert Owen, this early-19th-century current imagined ideal, non-capitalist societies but was later dismissed by Marxists as impractical — what is it called?
Utopian socialism: Political theory concerned with imagined socialist societies.
Before leading a nation through a full-scale invasion, this law graduate co-founded a comedy company called Kvartal 95 — which president took office in 2019?
Volodymyr Zelenskyy: President of Ukraine since 2019.

A vaudeville-trained humorist born a citizen of the Cherokee Nation and known as 'Oklahoma's Favorite Son,' he made 71 films and wrote over 4,000 newspaper columns before dying in a 1935 plane crash — who was he?
Will Rogers: American humorist and entertainer (1879–1935)
This Pakistani general became the country's third president under martial law in 1969, and his tenure oversaw the war that led to Bangladesh's independence — who was he?
Yahya Khan: President of Pakistan from 1969 to 1971.
Serving first as Albania's youngest-ever prime minister at 27, then president, then finally crowning himself monarch in 1928, this statesman ruled the country until 1939 — who was he?
Zog I: Leader of Albania from 1922 to 1939.
Which of these four is the eldest?

Oliver Heaviside (born 1850) is the earliest of the four. Although at odds with the scientific establishment for most of his life, Heaviside changed the face of telecommunications, mathematics, and science.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (born 1906) is the earliest of the four. In 1986, the Maria Goeppert Mayer Award for early-career women physicists was established in her honor.
Which of these four was founded earliest?

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Samuel C. C. Ting is a physicist.
Pick the chemist from these four.
What is the atomic number of Lawrencium?
Lawrencium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lr (formerly Lw) and atomic number 103.
In what year was Hypatia born?
Hypatia: Not the only fourth century Alexandrian female mathematician, Hypatia was preceded by Pandrosion.
In what year was Bertrand Russell born?
Bertrand Russell: Bertrand Arthur William Russell, 3rd Earl Russell (18 May 1872 – 2 February 1970), was an English philosopher, logician, mathematician, and public intellectual.
In what year was Ümit Özdağ born?
Ümit Özdağ: On 16 November 2020, Özdağ was also dismissed from the Good Party.
In what year did Hans Albert Einstein die?
Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.
In what year did John McAfee die?
John McAfee: In 1987, he wrote the first commercial anti-virus software, founding McAfee Associates to sell his creation.
In what year was Special relativity discovered?
Special relativity: In physics, the special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
In what year was Mustard gas discovered?
Mustard gas: There is no preventive agent against mustard gas, with protection depending entirely on skin and airways protection, and no antidote exists for mustard poisoning.
Sodium acetate: Pfizer. Sodium acetate is a chemical compound with formula CH3COONa, also abbreviated NaOAc.
Which country is Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider from?

Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider: United States. Part of the Long Range Strike Bomber (LRS-B) program, it is to be an intercontinental strategic bomber that can deliver conventional and thermonuclear weapons.
Who is credited with discovering Archaea?
Archaea: Carl Woese. Archaea (ar-KEE-ə) is a domain of organisms.
Who is credited with discovering Synapse?
Synapse: Charles Scott Sherrington. In the nervous system, a synapse is a structure that allows a neuron to exchange (receive or send) signals with another cell in its immediate vicinity.
Who is credited with discovering Nitrogen?
Nitrogen: Daniel Rutherford. Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Known by the abbreviation NAC, this mucolytic drug treats acetaminophen overdose and also loosens thick mucus in people with chronic lung conditions like pneumonia and bronchitis — which drug?

Acetylcysteine (NAC) is a mucolytic that is used to treat paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose and to loosen thick mucus in individuals with chronic bronchopulmonary disorders, such as pneumonia and bronchitis.
Believed to be an autoimmune attack that breaches the immune privilege of hair follicles, this condition typically leaves a few coin-sized bald spots on the scalp — what is it?
Alopecia areata (AA), also known as spot baldness, is a condition in which hair is lost from some or all areas of the body.
Best known for his laws of planetary motion, this German astronomer has also been called the 'father of science fiction' for his novel Somnium. Who is he?

Antelope is any of the extant or recently extinct species of the ruminant artiodactyl family Bovidae, which are indigenous to most of Africa, India, the Middle East, Central Asia, and a small area of Russia.
Doctors reach for this NSAID not just for aches but to treat Kawasaki disease and rheumatic fever — and it's famous for its blood-thinning effect on platelets. What is it?
Aspirin is the genericized trademark for acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to reduce pain, fever, and inflammation, and as an antithrombotic.

Found naturally in many plants and abbreviated "Bz," this white crystalline compound is the simplest of the aromatic carboxylic acids and lends its salts to the world of food preservatives — what is it?
Benzoic acid is a white or colorless crystalline organic compound with the formula C6H5COOH, whose structure consists of a benzene ring (C6H6) with a carboxyl (C(=O)OH) substituent.
This Russian mathematician-turned-oligarch was worth an estimated $3 billion in 1997 after privatizing state assets like Channel One — yet died impoverished and depressed in 2013. Who was he?
Boris Berezovsky (businessman) (23 January 1946 - 23 March 2013), also known as Platon Elenin, was a Russian business oligarch, government official, engineer and mathematician.
Atomic number 20 and chemically akin to strontium and barium, this metal is the most common ingredient in limestone — found there as its carbonate. What element?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
A first-generation cephalosporin that can be swallowed rather than infused, this antibiotic disrupts the bacterial cell wall to treat ear, skin and urinary infections — what is it?
Cefalexin is an antibiotic that can treat a number of bacterial infections. It kills gram-positive and some gram-negative bacteria by disrupting the growth of the bacterial cell wall.
Charted in 1756 by Lacaille and named for the drafting tool that draws circles, this faint southern constellation is easily confused with the mariner's-compass constellation Pyxis. Which one is it?
Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
First created in Germany in 1996 and named for an astronomer on his 537th birthday, this synthetic element (number 112) may even be a gas — which one?
Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.

Known for names like thornapple, jimsonweed, and devil's trumpet, this genus of nine extremely poisonous, night-blooming plants in the nightshade family can cause hallucinations and delirium if ingested — what is it?
Datura is a genus of nine species of highly poisonous, vespertine-flowering plants belonging to the nightshade family (Solanaceae).
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'female dragon,' and this genus of roughly 200 tree and shrub species now also includes what was once classified as Sansevieria — which genus is it?
Dracaena (plant) is a genus of about 200-220 species of trees and woody shrubs.
This branch of medicine studies the body's hormone-secreting glands and the chemical messengers, called hormones, that regulate growth, metabolism, mood, and more — name the field?
Endocrinology (from endocrine + -ology) is a branch of biology and medicine dealing with the endocrine system, its diseases, and its specific secretions known as hormones.
This Chinese-born American computer scientist built ImageNet, the dataset that supercharged computer vision in the 2010s, and co-directs Stanford's Human-Centered AI institute — who is she?

Fei-Fei Li (pinyin: L Fifi; born July 3, 1976) is a Chinese-born American computer scientist best known for establishing ImageNet, the dataset that enabled rapid advances in computer vision in the 2010s.
Named after a German militant group in a reader's 1994 letter and formalized by a Stanford linguist in 2005, this cognitive bias makes newly learned facts seem suddenly everywhere — what is it?

Frequency illusion (also known as the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon or Red Car Theory) is a cognitive bias in which a person notices a specific concept, word, or product more frequently after recently becoming aware of it.
The largest and outermost of the three hip muscles, this one shapes the buttocks and helps keep the human trunk upright — what muscle is it?
Gluteus maximus is the main extensor muscle of the hip in humans.

Element 108's isotope 270 carries magic numbers of protons and neutrons that shore it up against fission, yet the most stable forms last only about ten seconds — which synthetic superheavy element is it?
Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Running from the shoulder to the elbow, this arm bone connects the scapula to the radius and ulna, with a rounded head and neck at one end and two epicondyles at the other — name this bone?
Humerus (pl.: humeri) is a long bone in the arm that runs from the shoulder to the elbow.
Denoted by the symbol ∞, this concept of the boundless and endless has been debated by philosophers since ancient Greece and by mathematicians since the 17th century — what is it?
Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
Known as the sunroot or earth apple, this central-North-American member of the sunflower family is cultivated for its tuber rather than its bloom — what is it?
Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus), also called sunroot, sunchoke, wild sunflower, topinambur, or earth apple, is a species of sunflower native to central North America.
Native to Central and South American rainforests, this frugivorous nocturnal mammal related to raccoons and coatis shares its 'honey bear' nickname with an unrelated species — which animal?
Kinkajou (/kkdu/; Potos flavus) is a mammal of the family Procyonidae, a relative to olingos, coatis, raccoons, and the ringtail and cacomistle.
Used to treat an underactive thyroid and even a severe form called myxedema coma, this synthetic version of thyroxine (T4) takes about six weeks to reach a steady blood level — what's this drug?
Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4). It is used to treat thyroid hormone deficiency (hypothyroidism), including a severe form known as myxedema coma.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.
In hermaphroditic species this reproductive pairing isn't strictly required, since self-fertilization is possible — what is the general term for it?
Mating refers to the pairing of either opposite-sex or hermaphroditic organisms for the purpose of sexual reproduction.
First flown by the Soviet Air Force in 1968 and still in Russian production today, this medium chopper carries the NATO reporting name 'Hip' — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-8 is a family of medium twin-turbine helicopters, originally designed by the Soviet Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute (TsAGI) in the 1960s and introduced into the Soviet Air Force in 1968.

Caused when fly larvae burrow into and feed on an animal's tissue, this parasitic infestation is triggered by open wounds but can occur on unbroken skin when species such as the botfly are involved — name this condition?
Myiasis (my-), also known as flystrike or fly strike, is the parasitic infestation of the body of a live animal by fly larvae (maggots) that grow inside the host while feeding on its tissue.
This Danish-Norwegian eurodance group's 1997 single caused controversy and a lawsuit from a toy company over its double entendres about a certain plastic doll. Who are they?
North American XB-70 Valkyrie is a retired prototype version of the planned B-70 nuclear-armed, deep-penetration supersonic strategic bomber for the United States Air Force Strategic Air Command.
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compounds pairs oxygen with at least one other element — even the thin protective skin on aluminum foil counts as one — what's the class?
Oxide is a chemical compound containing at least one oxygen atom and one other element in its chemical formula.

Classically, one form of this condition wakes you at night with upper abdominal pain that eases when you eat, while another flares up after meals — and a third of older sufferers feel nothing at all. What is it?
Peptic ulcer disease refers to damage of the inner part of the stomach's gastric mucosa (lining of the stomach), the first part of the small intestine, or sometimes the lower esophagus.
This GABA-derived drug treats cognitive disorders, vertigo, and dyslexia, and shares its 'racetam' drug class with related compounds like levetiracetam and aniracetam — what is it?
Piracetam is a drug that has efficacy in cognitive disorders, vertigo, cortical myoclonus, dyslexia, and sickle cell anemia; sources differ on its usefulness for dementia.
Bloating, mood swings, breast tenderness and irritability that flare in the week or two before menstruation and fade once bleeding begins — what disruptive condition is this?
Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a disruptive set of emotional and physical symptoms that regularly occur in the one to two weeks before the start of each menstrual period.
This colorless, odorless radioactive noble gas has the atomic number 86, and its longest-lived isotope has a half-life of under four days — name the element?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
This big, sociable black corvid is told apart from its relatives by a bare, whitish patch on its face, and it nests in noisy treetop colonies near farms and villages — which bird is it?
Rook (bird) (Corvus frugilegus) is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds.

These colorful predatory marine animals — single polyps usually anchored by their base — are named after a terrestrial flower and, unlike their jellyfish relatives, skip the medusa stage entirely; what are they?
Sea anemone (-) are a group of predatory marine invertebrate animals constituting the order Actiniaria.
This group of nocturnal Southeast Asian primates ranges from Yunnan province in China down to the island of Java, with a pygmy relative recently reclassified into its own genus — what are they?
Slow loris are a group of several species of nocturnal strepsirrhine primates that make up the genus Nycticebus.
Innervated by the accessory nerve, which of the body's largest and most superficial neck structures rotates the head to the opposite side and flexes the neck?
Sternocleidomastoid muscle is one of the largest and most superficial cervical muscles.

A carnivorous marsupial formerly found across mainland Australia but now confined to Tasmania, this animal became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial after the thylacine's extinction in 1936. What is this fierce creature?
Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii; palawa kani: purinina) is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

Sitting at the organizational level between individual cells and a full organ, this biological term for a functional grouping of similar cells derives from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology) is an assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix from the same embryonic origin that together carry out a specific function.
A physician before politics, this German served as Angela Merkel's defence minister and in 2019 became President of the European Commission — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen (ne Albrecht; born 8 October 1958) is a German politician and physician who has served as President of the European Commission since 2019.
This small insect-eating songbird breeds across most of Europe and Asia, migrates to Africa in winter, and has a black-backed form that predominates in Britain and Ireland — what is it?
White wagtail (Motacilla alba) is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws.
The only living member of its entire mammalian order, this nocturnal African burrower uses its long snout and powerful claws to dig ants and termites out of their mounds — what animal is it?
Aardvark: Burrowing mammal native to Africa.
While bacteria and some plants may be biologically immortal, this universal process in humans slows reaction time even as knowledge tends to grow — what is it called?
Ageing: Biological process of getting older.
Though commonly called a nut, this tree's fruit is technically a drupe with a hard shell surrounding an edible seed, closely related to the peach — which food is it?
Almond: Species of nut. The fruit of the almond is a drupe, consisting of an outer hull and a hard shell with the seed, which is not a true nut.
This Manchester physicist shared the 2010 Nobel Prize for his work on graphene — and is the only person to also hold an Ig Nobel, won for levitating a frog with magnetism. Who is he?
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?
One of the oldest of the natural sciences, it leans on math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything from comets to quasars beyond Earth's atmosphere — what field is this?
Astronomy: Scientific study of celestial objects.
The most common type of skin cancer, this slow-growing tumor is sometimes called a 'rodent ulcer' and rarely spreads beyond its original site — what is it?
Basal-cell carcinoma: Most common type of skin cancer. Basal-cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as basal-cell cancer, basalioma, or rodent ulcer, is the most common type of skin cancer.
This field covers physiological traits like fingerprints and iris patterns, plus behavioral ones like typing rhythm and gait, all used to identify people — what is it called?
Biometrics: Metrics related to human characteristics.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
Surprisingly, the closest living relatives of birds are a clan of semiaquatic predators that includes alligators, caimans, and the long-snouted gharial. What is this reptile order?
Crocodilia: Order of reptiles. The teeth are conical and peg-like, and the bite is powerful.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.
Often triggered by contaminated food, NSAIDs, or autoimmune conditions like coeliac disease, which medical term describes inflammation of the small intestine?
Enteritis: Inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.

With a wingspan reaching 188 centimeters and distinctive ear tufts atop mottled blackish-and-tawny plumage, this raptor is one of the largest of its nocturnal kind, ranging widely across Europe and Asia — what bird is it?
Eurasian eagle-owl: Species of owl. The Eurasian eagle-owl (Bubo bubo) is a species of eagle-owl, a type of bird that resides much over Eurasia.

An annual legume with leaves of three small leaflets, this semiarid crop has flavored dishes of the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — yet there's little clinical proof it works as the supplement people often take. What is it?
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.

This digestive disorder involves weak stomach muscle contractions that delay how quickly food empties into the intestine, often linked to nerve damage from uncontrolled diabetes — what's the condition called?
Gastroparesis: Medical condition. The opposite of this, where stomach contents exit quickly into the duodenum, is called dumping syndrome.
As the single largest muscle in the human body, this hip extensor gives the buttocks their shape and is a key reason humans can stand upright, unlike other primates — what is it?
Gluteus maximus: Largest and most superficial of the three gluteal muscles.
Breeders prefer to call it a 'cavy,' and despite its name it hails from the Andes rather than West Africa and isn't related to swine at all — which Andean rodent is it?
Guinea pig: Domesticated rodent from South America.
Comprising cicadas, aphids, bed bugs, and more than 80,000 other species with piercing-sucking mouthparts, which insect order is nicknamed the 'true bugs'?
Hemiptera: Order of insects often called true bugs.
First published as a Latin anagram in 1676 by a British physicist, this principle states that the force needed to stretch a spring scales linearly with its extension — which law?
Hooke's law: Force needed to pull a spring grows linearly with distance.

Affecting roughly one in 250 baby boys, this is the second most common birth defect of the male reproductive system, in which a key opening doesn't form in its usual place — what is this condition called?
Hypospadias: Malformation in which the urethral opening is misplaced.
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
Built from an umbrella-shaped bell of mesoglea that pulses to swim, this Cnidarian trails stinging tentacles and is the medusa phase of its complex life cycle — what is it?
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this bumpy-skinned citrus fruit is prized in regional cooking for its intensely fragrant leaves and rind, and its oil is used in perfumery — which fruit?
Kaffir lime: Citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia. Citrus hystrix, called the kaffir lime, Thai lime or makrut lime, (US:, UK:) is a citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia.
Making up 2 to 8 percent of milk by mass, this disaccharide combines galactose and glucose and takes its name from the Latin word for milk — what is it?
Lactose: Carbohydrate. Lactose is a disaccharide composed of galactose and glucose and has the molecular formula C12H22O11.
Also sold as Xylocaine, this amino-amide local anesthetic numbs in minutes and doubles as a treatment for dangerous ventricular heart rhythms — what is it?
Lidocaine: Local anesthetic. Lidocaine, also known as lignocaine and sold under the brand name Xylocaine among others, is a local anesthetic of the amino amide type.

Credited as a 'Father of Cinematography,' this French artist filmed the Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888 — then vanished without a trace two years later, and his work never shaped commercial cinema. Who was he?
Louis Le Prince: French motion-picture pioneer (1841–1890s)
Distinguished from living elephants by spirally twisted tusks and a thick coat of fur for cold climates, this extinct genus survived from the late Miocene until roughly 4,000 years ago — what was it?
Mammoth: Extinct genus of mammals. The oldest mammoth representative, Mammuthus subplanifrons, appeared around 6 million years ago during the late Miocene in southern and Eastern Africa.
Home to the heart, esophagus, trachea, thymus, and central chest lymph nodes, this compartment of the thoracic cavity sits between the lungs — what's it called?
Mediastinum: Central part of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum (from Medieval Latin: mediastinus, lit. 'midway';pl.: mediastina) is the central compartment of the thoracic cavity.
Son of a U.S. vice president, this young art collector vanished in 1961 during an expedition into New Guinea's Asmat region, with some accounts claiming he was killed by local tribesmen — who was he?
Michael Rockefeller: American anthropologist and art collector (1938–1961)
Originally a dry-season staple for ǃKung hunter-gatherers, this tropical vine in the Cucurbitaceae family produces an intensely bitter edible fruit widely used across Asian cuisine — what is it?
Momordica charantia: Species of plant in the gourd family.
Found in cardiac and skeletal muscle and distantly related to hemoglobin, high levels of this oxygen-storing protein let diving whales and seals hold their breath longer — which protein?
Also known as black cumin or kalonji, this flowering plant native to the Levant and Iran is used across the world as a culinary spice — which species is it?
Nigella sativa: Species of flowering plant in the buttercup family.
Native to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this striped mammal looks like a zebra crossbred with a giraffe but is actually the giraffe's closest living relative — which animal?
Okapi: Species of mammal. Although the okapi has striped markings reminiscent of zebras, it is most closely related to the giraffe.
A reactive nonmetal of the chalcogen group, it's the most abundant element in Earth's crust — locked into water, silicates, and rust — and the third-most abundant in the universe. What is it?
Oxygen: Chemical element with atomic number 8 (O)
Carl Linnaeus named this crop 'hypogaea' — Greek for 'under the earth' — because, unlike most legumes, it ripens its pods below ground. What is it?
Peanut: Legume cultivated as a grain and oil crop.
Its name combines the Greek words for 'love' and 'tree,' and with over 600 accepted species it's the second-largest genus in the arum family after Anthurium — which popular houseplant genus?
Known informally for resembling a certain dairy product due to its shape, this popular edible fungus grows wild across temperate and subtropical forests worldwide — what is its scientific name?
First prescribed in 1934, this steroid sex hormone plays a key role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development — what is it?
Progesterone: Sex hormone. Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
This is the name for three positive whole numbers a, b, and c satisfying a² + b² = c², like the classic set (3, 4, 5) — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple: Integer side lengths of a right triangle.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
